# terraform-provider-waroom

The [Waroom](https://waroom.com/) Provider enables Terraform to manage [Waroom](https://waroom.com/) resources.

## Docs

### Implement a provider with the Terraform Plugin Framework

This is the official HashiCorp documentation, providing a comprehensive guide for implementing Terraform providers.
Our implementation follows this documentation for implementation details, best practices, and standards.

## Project Structure

### Core Components

- `internal/provider/`: Provider implementation
  - `provider.go`: Main provider configuration and setup
  - `data_source_*.go`: Data source implementations
  - `resource_*.go`: Resource implementations
  - `provider_test.go`: Shared test setup (provider factories for acceptance tests)

### Implemented Resources and Data Sources

- The registered resources / data sources are listed in `Resources()` / `DataSources()` in `provider.go`; their docs are in `docs/resources/` and `docs/data-sources/`.
- `waroom_service_label` (`resource_service_label.go`, `data_source_service_label.go`) is the reference implementation for new ones (CRUD + import under a parent service).

### Key Dependencies

- **Terraform Plugin Framework**: v1.19.0
- **Waroom Client SDK**: `github.com/topotal/waroom-client-go` (pre-1.0; the API may change)
  - The version pinned in `go.mod` is what CI builds against. A local `go.work` (gitignored) may point to `../waroom-client-go`, which can contain unreleased APIs. To check what the pinned version provides, use `GOWORK=off` (e.g. `GOWORK=off go mod download -json github.com/topotal/waroom-client-go@<version>` for its source directory).
- **Go Version**: 1.27.4

### Development Tools

- **Task Runner**: Uses [Taskfile](https://taskfile.dev/) for common operations
  - `task gen name=<name> [kind=resource|data_source]`: Generate new resource / data source scaffolding
  - `task gen:r name=<name>`: Generate resource (shortcut)
  - `task gen:d name=<name>`: Generate data source (shortcut)
  - `task build`: Build the project
  - `task test`: Run unit tests
  - `task test:acc`: Run acceptance tests (requires E2E_WAROOM_API_KEY and E2E_WAROOM_API_ENDPOINT)
  - `task test:acc:op`: Run acceptance tests with the variables from the per-developer `.env.e2e` (template: `.env.e2e.example`), resolved by the 1Password CLI. Never ask for or print these values
  - `task fmt`: Format code
  - `task lint`: Run linter

- **Code Generator**: `cmd/tfgen` - Custom tool for generating resource / data source boilerplate

- **Claude Code skills** (`.claude/skills/`)
  - `/client-coverage`: Compare the pinned client API with the implemented resources / data sources, and file one issue per missing candidate
  - `/implement-candidate <issue>`: Implement a candidate issue in a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/`, through acceptance tests, docs and a PR

### Tracking Resource / Data Source Coverage

- Each candidate resource / data source has an issue labeled `resource-candidate`, with a marker in its body: `<!-- client-coverage: kind=<resource|data_source> name=<waroom_xxx> -->`. Issues are sub-issues of the tracking issue #38.
- To decide not to support a candidate, comment the reason and **Close as not planned**. `/client-coverage` keeps listing these with their reasons.
- When adding a resource / data source by hand, reference its `resource-candidate` issue (`Closes #<n>`) so the coverage report stays accurate.

## Implementation Guidelines

### When Adding New Resources

1. Use `task gen:r name=<resource_name>` to generate scaffolding
2. Implement CRUD operations following existing patterns in `resource_service_label.go`
3. Add unit tests and acceptance tests
4. Follow Terraform Plugin Framework documentation (linked above)
5. Use the Waroom Client SDK (`waroom-client-go`) for API interactions

### Testing Approach

- **Unit Tests**: Standard Go tests using testify assertions
- **Acceptance Tests**: Use Terraform's testing framework with `TF_ACC=1`
- Always test the full CRUD lifecycle and import functionality
- E2E tests require valid Waroom API credentials

### Error Handling

- Handle 404 errors appropriately (e.g., remove from state in Read operations). API errors are returned as `*waroom.APIError` (wrapped), so check the status code with `errors.As`:
  ```go
  var apiErr *waroom.APIError
  if errors.As(err, &apiErr) && apiErr.StatusCode == http.StatusNotFound {
      resp.State.RemoveResource(ctx)
      return
  }
  ```
  When Read has to use a `List` API (no `Get`), treat "not found in the list" as 404.
- Use Terraform's diagnostic system for error reporting
- Log important operations using terraform-plugin-log
